findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_appeal_precedents" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Semantic search over UK planning appeal decision letters — Planning Inspectorate (England), PEDW (Wales), DPEA (Scotland), PAC (Northern Ireland): given a natur…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_application_record · Private data: get_application, get_application_record, list_application_documents, quote_application_documents, search_applications, aggregate_applications, search_appeal_precedents, get_application_appeals, list_appeals, get_appeal, search_policies, get_search_coverage · Public sink: get_application_record, get_search_coverage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_application_record · Private data: get_application, get_application_record, list_application_documents, quote_application_documents, search_applications, aggregate_applications, search_appeal_precedents, get_application_appeals, list_appeals, get_appeal, search_policies, get_search_coverage · Public sink: get_application_record, get_search_coverage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
